land.text: the island of Dominica: 'In 1763, France lost the war and ceded the island to Great Britain in 1763 under the Treaty of Paris'

predecessors.note: Britain first 'conquered the island' in 1761 and the 1783 Treaty of Paris 'returned the island to British control' (Dominica page). The dossier starts at the Associated State date, 1 March 1967, as the sibling dossiers of Grenada, Saint Vincent and Antigua and Barbuda do; Cliopatria's own row begins in 1979. The colony itself has no dossier yet.

capitals.name: Roseau
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Roseau 15°18′N 61°23′W'; 'The capital, Roseau, is located on the western side of the island.' The page does not date the seat; the coordinates are the gazetteer's Natural Earth point, which agrees with the infobox.

correction.text: the island of Dominica, an Associated State of the United Kingdom from 1 March 1967 and independent from 3 November 1978: 'Dominica comprises a land area of 750 km2'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Commonwealth of Dominica row begins in 1979, twelve years after the island became an Associated State (1 March 1967) and a year after independence (3 November 1978). The country outline is used; the page gives 750 km2 and the grid resolves the country to 3 cells (about 759 km2).

correction.text: the island of Dominica: 'Dominica comprises a land area of 750 km2'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 7-vertex polygon is 1,262.9 km2 against the infobox 750 km2 (ratio 1.68, within a factor of two) and its bbox (-61.48..-61.15, 15.20..15.65) is the island's. On the 253 km2 grid the polygon resolves to 2 cells (about 506 km2) and leaves out the north-western cell that Natural Earth's outline holds (3 cells, about 759 km2, the infobox figure to within 1 %), so the correction names the country. Same island through 2023; no border moves.

correction.text: the island of Dominica: 'Dominica comprises a land area of 750 km2'

keyframe_review.note: Identical to the 1979 shape (1,262.9 km2); same correction. The page lists no change of land borders since independence.

region.text: the island of Dominica, an Associated State of the United Kingdom with internal self-government

ledger.note: 1 March 1967: Dominica becomes an Associated State of the United Kingdom. 'Dominica became an associated state of the United Kingdom in 1967, and formally took responsibility for its internal affairs'; infobox 'West Indies Associated States: 1 March 1967'. The West Indies Associated States page gives the same date and says the UK 'retained responsibility for external affairs and defence'; that client relation (1967-1978) belongs in the British Colonial Empire dossier as a vassal_start/vassal_end naming this state.

3 November 1978: Dominica becomes independent. 'On 3 November 1978, Dominica was granted independence as a republic, led by Prime Minister Patrick John.' Same island and colour; the West Indies Associated States page gives the same date as the end of the association. Cliopatria's row begins the next year, 1979.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border and there is no land boundary. The maritime dispute with Venezuela over the sea around Isla de Aves ('unofficially ending the territorial claim' in June 2006) is not territory on the map.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Dominica, West Indies Associated States). Start year: Cliopatria's row begins in 1979, but the island became an Associated State on 1 March 1967 and independent on 3 November 1978; the dossier starts in March 1967 as the am-08-k siblings grenada, saint-vincent and antigua-and-barbuda do, and a 1967-1978 keyframe fills the years Cliopatria lacks. The 1978 independence is a rename (status change), not a new state. Cliopatria's polygon (2 grid cells) is a subset of Natural Earth's Dominica (3 cells; the missing cell is the north-west end), hence adjust verdicts naming the country. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row still touches Dominica until 1995 (seed neighbours 1979-1995), so eu-11 should release the island in 1967 as an Associated State (vassal_start naming commonwealth-of-dominica, 1 March 1967) and vassal_end 3 November 1978. The pre-1967 colony (British since the Treaty of Paris, 1763; part of a short-lived West Indies Federation province from 1958 per the Dominica page) has no dossier: suggested slug colony-of-dominica, for am-08-x or eu-11. Considered and left out: the 1981 coup attempts and mercenary plot (no border effect), Hurricane David 1979, the Aves Island maritime dispute with Venezuela (sea, undated start; the page only says it was 'long-running' and that the prime minister conceded Aves Island in June 2006). No ruler list: the head of state changed with the republic; a documented list was not opened.
